1.outline: Term theme: 'Slides & Digital Citizens'. Plan a narrated slide story on paper before building it on screen: what happens on each slide.
1.sowResources: Printed storyboard sheet, exemplar slide story.
objectives: Plan a story across several slides.
Sketch what happens on each slide.
Explain my story plan to a partner.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Watch an exemplar
plan.detail: Watch a short slide-story exemplar and notice how it's split into scenes.

plan.title: Storyboard
plan.detail: Plan 4-5 slides on paper: what happens, what picture, one line of narration each.

plan.title: Pitch it
plan.detail: Tell a partner your story plan in 30 seconds. Log out.

successCriteria: My storyboard has 4-5 planned slides.
Each slide has a picture idea and a line of narration.
I can pitch my story plan to a partner.

2.outline: Turn the storyboard into real slides, adding one image per scene from the class picture folder or own drawings.
2.sowResources: Google Slides, PowerPoint, class picture folder.
objectives: Create a slide for each planned scene.
Insert an image on each slide.
Follow the storyboard plan.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Build the scenes
plan.detail: Create a slide for each storyboard scene and insert a matching image.

plan.title: Order check
plan.detail: Check the slides are in the right story order. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I created a slide for each planned scene.
Each slide has a matching image.
My slides follow the storyboard order.

3.outline: Add transitions between scenes and think about pacing — does the story flow smoothly from one slide to the next?
objectives: Add consistent transitions between slides.
Judge whether the story flows smoothly.
Adjust slide order or content if it doesn't flow.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Add transitions
plan.detail: Apply one consistent transition style across all slides.

plan.title: Flow check
plan.detail: Play the deck through — does it make sense as a story? Adjust anything that jumps oddly.

plan.title: Peer flow test
plan.detail: A partner watches the deck play and says if the story made sense. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My slides use one consistent transition.
My story flows in a sensible order.
A partner understood my story when it played through.

4.outline: Write speaker notes for each scene so the story can be narrated aloud when presented.
objectives: Write narration notes for each slide.
Keep notes short and speakable, not a full script.
Practise reading the notes aloud with the slide.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Write narration
plan.detail: Write one or two narration sentences per slide in the notes area.

plan.title: Practise aloud
plan.detail: Read through the whole story aloud using the notes as prompts, not a script to read word for word.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: Every slide has narration notes.
My notes are short prompts, not a full script.
I practised narrating the whole story aloud.

5.outline: Play Google's Interland 'Tower of Treasure' to learn what makes a strong password, then write down one password rule.
5.sowResources: Google Interland (Tower of Treasure), password-rule cards.
objectives: Play Tower of Treasure and identify strong vs weak passwords.
Explain one rule for a strong password.
Explain why a strong password matters.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Tower of Treasure
plan.detail: Play the Interland game, discussing password choices as they come up.

plan.title: Password rules
plan.detail: As a class, list what makes a password strong: length, mixing letters/numbers, not using your name.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Each pupil writes one password rule on a card. Log out.

successCriteria: I played Tower of Treasure and made sensible choices.
I can explain one rule for a strong password.
I can explain why strong passwords matter.

6.outline: Revisit Google Interland's 'Kind Kingdom' ideas about being kind online, and discuss what cyber-kindness looks like in everyday life.
objectives: Recall the Kind Kingdom rules about online kindness.
Give an example of cyber-kindness.
Explain what to do if someone is unkind online.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Kind Kingdom recap
plan.detail: Play or recall the Kind Kingdom scenarios and discuss the choices.

plan.title: Cyber-kindness examples
plan.detail: In pairs, come up with one example of being kind online and one example of unkindness.

plan.title: What to do
plan.detail: Discuss: if someone is unkind online, tell a trusted adult. Log out.

successCriteria: I can recall a Kind Kingdom rule.
I gave an example of cyber-kindness.
I know to tell a trusted adult about online unkindness.

7.outline: Finish and polish the whole slide story: check images, transitions, narration and overall flow one more time.
objectives: Complete every slide of the story.
Polish images, transitions and narration.
Check the whole story makes sense start to finish.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Polish pass
plan.detail: Go through every slide fixing anything unfinished: missing images, missing notes, inconsistent transitions.

plan.title: Full play-through
plan.detail: Play the whole story from start to finish and check it makes sense.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save the finished story. Log out.

successCriteria: Every slide is complete with an image and notes.
My transitions are consistent throughout.
My story makes sense from start to finish.

8.outline: Present the finished slide story to a small group and give two-stars-and-a-wish feedback to a classmate.
objectives: Present a slide story using narration notes.
Give two stars and a wish for a classmate's story.
Explain a strong-password rule when asked.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Small-group presentations
plan.detail: Present the story to a small group using narration notes, not reading the slide word for word.

plan.title: Two stars and a wish
plan.detail: Each listener gives two things they liked and one kind improvement suggestion.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Save the finished story to the portfolio folder. Log out.

successCriteria: I presented my story using my narration notes.
I gave a classmate two stars and a wish.
I explained one strong-password rule.

9.outline: Extend the finished story with one extra scene, applying feedback received from the presentation.
objectives: Add one new scene to the story.
Apply at least one piece of feedback received.
Keep the new scene consistent with the rest of the story.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Extend the story
plan.detail: Add a new scene, applying at least one wish from the feedback received last lesson.

plan.title: Consistency check
plan.detail: Check the new scene matches the style of the rest. Save.

plan.title: Log out
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: My story now has an extra scene.
I applied at least one piece of feedback.
The new scene matches the rest of the story.

10.outline: Rehearse the term's slide-story skills in pairs: plan, build, add narration, present.
10.sowResources: Recap slide deck, practice task cards.
objectives: Recall the term's slide-story process in order.
Rehearse building and narrating a short slide.
Identify the trickiest step.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Process recap
plan.detail: Recap: plan, build, transitions, narration, present — as a class chant.

plan.title: Paired rehearsal
plan.detail: Build and narrate one short slide with a partner, then swap.

plan.title: Tricky step check
plan.detail: Name the step you still find hardest. Log out.

successCriteria: I can list the term's slide-story steps in order.
I rehearsed building and narrating with a partner.
I know which step needs more practice.

11.outline: Individual task: plan and build a short narrated slide story with images, a consistent transition and speaker notes, and explain one strong-password rule.
objectives: Plan and build a short slide story independently.
Add narration/notes and images.
Explain one strong-password rule.

plan.title: Settle and explain
plan.detail: Calm start — explain the task and rubric.

plan.title: Build the story
plan.detail: Individual practical: plan and build 3-4 slides with images and narration notes.

plan.title: Password question
plan.detail: One-to-one: 'tell me one rule for a strong password.'

plan.title: Save and celebrate
plan.detail: Save the story and celebrate the term's progress. Log out.

successCriteria: I planned and built a short slide story on my own.
My story has images and narration notes.
I explained one strong-password rule.
